newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Kelley urges greater clearinghouse security.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Kelley urges greater clearinghouse security.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Edward Kelley said on Tuesday that the central bank welcomes efforts by banks and clearinghouse associations to curb risks in the systems they use for making payments.

"It has often been the clearinghouse participants themselves that have designed and pressed for the most innovative and effective tools for risk management," Kelley said in a speech prepared for delivery to a conference on payments system risk.
"We would welcome further steps along these lines," he added.

Clearinghouses, along with banks and the Fed, play a vital role in completing payments that can be made in a variety of ways from writing a check to electronic transfer and that are completed by a transfer of funds between parties.

Many potential risks exist, ranging from lack of liquidity if settlement payments are delayed to legal and security risks arising from growing use of new technologies like stored-value cards and Internet-based payments systems.
The Fed currently offers a same-day net settlement service for national clearinghouses in which they use the Fedwire to transfer funds to complete settlements each day.
Kelley said some have asked whether the benefit of reduced risks offered through the Fedwire settlement service could be provided in a more convenient format.

"The Federal Reserve staff is actively reviewing this possibility along with the Board's general risk policies relating to smaller-dollar clearing arrangements," Kelley said, adding, "I think that there will be good progress to report on these issues relatively early next year."
